Scientists may have just discovered 115-million-year-old dinosaur blood inside a fossilized bone. But what if we could actually extract living cells from it? Realistically, DNA completely breaks down after about seven million years, making Jurassic Park-style cloning impossible. However, intact prehistoric proteins and red blood cells could reveal how giant dinosaurs fought off deadly viruses and survived extreme climates. Could ancient dinosaur immunity hold secrets for modern medicine? Tell us what you think below, and follow for more what-ifs!
